name: @corlabsdev/mcp

tools.name: cor_open
tools.description: Open a URL in the COR-controlled browser. The browser starts on first use and is reused across calls. For a page behind a login, pass a Playwright storage-state file so the existing session is adopted. The reply lists the page's controls with refs (on a large page, a region index) — no cor_snapshot needed first — and, when the project's code already uses COR entries for this page, which members those are and whether each still finds its element.

storageState.description: Path to a Playwright storage-state JSON file ({cookies, origins}) — e.g. from `npx playwright codegen --save-storage`.

tools.name: cor_click
tools.description: Click an element to reach a page state — open a menu, go to the next step. Does not assert anything.

ref.description: Element ref from the latest cor_snapshot, e.g. "e4". Alternative to target.

target.description: CSS selector for the element — must match exactly one. Alternative to ref.

tools.name: cor_fill
tools.description: Set the value of an input, textarea, select or editable element, firing input and change events.

ref.description: Element ref from the latest cor_snapshot, e.g. "e4". Alternative to target.

target.description: CSS selector for the element — must match exactly one. Alternative to ref.

tools.name: cor_press
tools.description: Press a key, e.g. Enter, Escape, Tab, ArrowDown. With a ref or target, that element is focused first.

key.description: Key name as Playwright spells it: Enter, Escape, Tab, ArrowDown, a, Shift+Tab.

ref.description: Element ref from the latest cor_snapshot, e.g. "e4". Alternative to target.

target.description: CSS selector for the element — must match exactly one. Alternative to ref.

tools.name: cor_close
tools.description: Close the browser and forget the session. The next cor_open starts a fresh one.

tools.name: cor_snapshot
tools.description: Outline of the visible interactive elements on the current page, each with a ref (e1, e2…), nested only under what identifies it: landmarks, sections by heading, tables (column / row), list items. Pick the element you need, then pass its ref to cor_inspect. Markers: ✓id test attribute, +N hidden lookalikes, [disabled]/[checked]/[expanded]/[selected], [unstable id]; "clickable" is an element with no role that the page makes clickable (cursor: pointer). Take a new snapshot after any navigation or act call — earlier refs expire. On a large page it answers with a region index (each region's controls, the named ones first); full: true lists every control.

full.description: The whole outline even on a large page, instead of the region index.

within.description: Show one region in full instead — every line of text, prices and labels included. A ref (its region: the card, row, column or section that identifies it) or a region's name (a heading, a landmark label, a list item or table row's text). A name matching several regions returns the choices.

tools.name: cor_inspect
tools.description: Rank, score and match-count locators for one element, rendered for the chosen test framework. Pass a ref from cor_snapshot, or a CSS selector that matches exactly one element — or targets: many of them in one call, one entry each. The response leads with the recommendation; below the quality floor it recommends an application change (a test attribute) instead of a fragile locator. Use the locator as given; write the surrounding test code yourself.

ref.description: Element ref from the latest cor_snapshot, e.g. "e4".

selector.description: CSS or Playwright selector (:text-is, >>, text=) matching exactly one element — alternative to ref.

targets.description: P2a: several refs or selectors at once — every element you need from this page in one call. Each gets its entry only (no alternatives); inspect one ref alone for the detail.

framework.description: Test framework to render and rank for. Default: the project's framework as cor_open reported it, else playwright.

detail.description: P4: the full reply — alternatives, facts, why this order, the durable annotation. By default: the answer and its code, about 6 lines.

all.description: List every alternative. By default: the runner-up and the best of each other locator kind, up to 3.

tools.name: cor_grade
tools.description: Diagnose a selector that already exists — from a test file, a failing test, or a pull request — against the open page. When a test fails on a locator, call this FIRST, before re-identifying the element. It says whether the locator is broken (matches nothing), ambiguous (matches several), fragile, or healthy. If it reports Healthy, STOP: the locator is not why the test failed — look at the product or the assertion instead of replacing it. Accepts a CSS selector, an XPath, page.getByRole/getByText/getByLabel/getByPlaceholder/getByTestId/getByAltText/getByTitle(…) or page.locator('…') — chained with .locator/.getBy*/.filter({ has, hasNot, hasText, hasNotText, visible })/.or()/.and()/.first()/.last()/.nth(n) — cy.get('…') or cy.contains(…), chained with .find/.filter/.not/.closest/.parent/.children/.contains/.eq/.first/.last — $('…') / $$('…') with a WebdriverIO selector (CSS, XPath, tag=text, tag.class=text, *=text), chained with .$/.$$/[n]/.parentElement() and .filter/.find((el) => el.isDisplayed() | (await el.getText()) === … | (await el.$(…).isExisting())).

selector.description: The selector exactly as written in the test, e.g. page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }) or cy.get('.btn').

framework.description: Framework to render alternatives for. Default: the framework of the project as cor_open reported it, else the form of the selector (getBy* → playwright, cy.* → cypress), else playwright.

param.description: For a parameterised helper: the variable in the selector (e.g. title in getByText(title, { exact: true })). COR runs the locator for every value and says which items no value reaches.

values.description: Values to run the parameterised locator with. Omit to let COR find each item's values on the page (needs the chain to start with page.locator('css')).

tools.name: cor_check
tools.description: Run before the tests. Scans the test and locator files changed on this branch (or all: true for the whole project) and fails any locator without a COR id (the // COR cor:… comment an entry carries), any id COR did not issue here, and any positional pick (.first(), .nth(), .eq(), [n]). With the locator's page open it returns the fix: COR's entry to paste, or the id to add for a locator COR already has a record of.

files.description: Files to check, relative to the project root. Default: changed files.

all.description: Check every file in the project instead of the changed ones.

tools.name: cor_heal
tools.description: When a test fails because a locator no longer finds its element. Pass the locator line as it is in the file (its // COR cor:… comment included) or its id, with the page open where the element should be. COR opens the committed record for that id, tries the locators it recorded while this one worked, then the element's fingerprint, and proposes a graded replacement — or declines. It never edits a file. With no id, it lists the elements on this page whose recorded locators all fail.

locator.description: The broken locator line, its cor: comment included.

id.description: The entry's id (the 6 characters after cor:).

tools.name: cor_explore
tools.description: Discovery in one call: a list of steps, run in order — { open: url }, { click: ref|selector }, { fill: ref|selector, value }, { press: key, target? }, { inspect: ref|selector|[…] }, { within: region }, { expect: "exact text shown" }. Each step replies as its own tool would; refs from one step work in the next until a step opens a new page. No conditions or loops. It stops at the first step that fails (an element that is not exactly one, text not shown) and returns what ran, the page's region index with refs, and the step to resume from (resumeFrom). Put static elements first and the step that navigates away last.

click.description: Click a ref or a CSS selector matching one element (cor_click).

fill.description: Fill a ref or a CSS selector (cor_fill) with value.

press.description: Press a key (cor_press), on target when given.

target.description: For press: the ref or selector to focus first.

inspect.description: A ref or selector, or several (cor_inspect targets).

within.description: A region's text, controls and entries (cor_snapshot within).

expect.description: Text that must be shown on the page now, exactly.

resumeFrom.description: Skip to this step number (1-based) — from a previous stopped run.

instructions:
COR finds, checks and grades locators on a live page and gives you entries to place. Workflow:
1. cor_open the page: the reply lists its controls with refs (a region index on a large page — cor_snapshot within a region for its text, controls and entries).
2. Get every element you need in one call: cor_inspect targets: [refs]. To see what an action changes, act (cor_click, cor_fill, cor_press; many steps: cor_explore) and read the reply: it lists changed and new text, new page headings, with entries. Do not write scripts to read the page.
3. Place each entry as given, its // COR cor:… comment included, in the file it names. An entry taking a parameter (title, question) is one function for every item: write one function that takes the parameter, not a locator per item; when the test covers every item, loop over the every-item locator instead of typing the values. A · label member is what you click for a hidden input; assert the input's checked state.
4. Every locator comes from COR, including elements you only assert on. Never match by partial text (*=, a substring cy.contains, getByText without exact). Pass a locator you wrote or extended yourself to cor_grade, with param when it takes one (a step added to a template can match several elements inside an item); keep the page open — no cor_close — until you have graded them.
5. Before running the tests, run cor_check: it fails on any locator without a COR id and returns the entry to paste. An existing method for the element: fix it in place rather than adding a second one.
6. Assert what an action changed — the new text, the URL, that gone items are not displayed — with a retrying assertion, not a fixed sleep.
7. A test failing on a locator: cor_grade it; broken → cor_heal with its cor: line, and apply the proposal only if it is the same element.
Put independent calls in one turn: each turn re-reads the whole conversation.
In your final summary, list each locator you used with its COR score and the runner-up.
stderr: COR sends anonymous usage metrics (tool names, timings, outcomes). Turn off with COR_TELEMETRY=off. Details: README.
